metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Full participant Thursday
metadata.description: Sinnott (ribs) upgraded to full participation at Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott has regained health after kicking off Week 5 prep with a limited session Wednesday. He's expected to continue working in a depth role Sunday against the Giants behind Chig Okonkwo (hamstring), who was limited at practice both Wednesday and Thursday. Sinnott failed to step up when Okonkwo missed two games earlier this season.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott (elbow) a full participant Thursday
metadata.description: Ben Sinnott (elbow) was a full participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran tight end was able to log a full practice session on Thursday, despite being limited by an elbow injury on Wednesday. He should be good to go for Week 5 but doesn't project to be a relevant fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott (rib) limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Ben Sinnott (rib) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: To no surprise, Sinnott was limited at practice on Wednesday due to his nagging rib issue. He remains off of the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future, however.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Sinnott (ribs) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: With Chig Okonkwo back from his hamstring injury last Sunday against the Colts, Sinnott logged just 24 of 64 offensive snaps and wasn't targeted in the passing game. Lightyears from fantasy relevance, Sinnott has one catch for six yards across four appearances this season.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott (rib) practices Wednesday
metadata.description: Ben Sinnott practiced on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott remains off the fantasy radar when he is healthy.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Cleared for Week 4
metadata.description: Sinnott (ribs) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Colts.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott has no fantasy value, especially with Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) cleared to return against Indianapolis after missing the previous two contests. Sinnott has one catch for six yards on two targets across three appearances this season.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott (rib) considered limited Thursday
metadata.description: Ben Sinnott (rib) was considered a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott is still dealing with a rib issue of some kind and was a limited participant on Thursday again as a result. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant moving forward, however, regardless of whether or not he is healthy.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Limited at Thursday's practice
metadata.description: Sinnott (ribs) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Both Sinnott and Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) remained limited Thursday after being estimated as limited participants during Wednesday's walkthrough. Sinnott failed to capitalize on Okonkwo's absence over the previous two games, recording just one catch for six yards on two targets over that span. If Sinnott suits up Sunday against the Colts, most of his contributions will come as a blocker.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Limited with rib injury
metadata.description: Sinnott (ribs) was estimated as limited in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott played 34 offensive snaps in the upset win over the Seahawks in Week 3, and now his status is in some question heading into the Commanders' matchup with the Colts in London on Sunday. While Sinnott earned a limited designation Washington, the Commanders merely held a walkthrough. Sinnott's status will particularly bear monitoring the rest of the week, as Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) remains questionable after missing the last two games.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott (rib) limited participant Wednesday
metadata.description: Ben Sinnott (rib) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott is a new addition to San Francisco's injury report, being listed with a rib injury of some kind that left him limited at practice on Wednesday. He will continue to be irrelevant from a fantasy perspective moving forward, however, especially with Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) seemingly drawing close to a return to the lineup for Washington.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott sees one target in Week 3
metadata.description: Ben Sinnott failed to catch his only target in the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott has been non existent in the Washington offense to begin the season, recording one target or less in each of the first three games. The tight end remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Indianapolis Colts.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott A Dart Throw for Week 3 Against Seattle
metadata.description: Washington Commanders tight end Ben Sinnott played the second-highest snap share of his career (67.6%) in Week 2 against the Cowboys. In place of Chig Okonkwo (hamstring), Sinnott started and caught a ball for six yards on the team's first offensive snap of the game. However, that was the third-year tight end's only reception. Sinnott should be expected to see another high snap share in Week 3. Washington's offensive ceiling is lower without Jayden Daniels (elbow), but both of Sinnott's career touchdowns have come from Marcus Mariota. Facing the vaunted Seattle Seahawks defense in Week 3, Sinnott profiles as a desperation tight end option in Week 3, ranking as RotoBaller's TE51.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Catches sole target in loss
metadata.description: Sinnott caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 37-20 loss to the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott played 48 of the Commanders' 71 offensive snaps as well as nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The tight end started due to Chig Okonkwo's (hamstring) absence and was the primary blocker for many of the team's plays.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott A Deep Sleeper in Week 2 at Dallas
metadata.description: Washington Commanders tight end Ben Sinnott is expected to see a larger role in Week 2 against the Dallas Cowboys with Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) ruled out. Sinnott played only 26.9% of the snaps and didn't see a target on 10 routes in Week 1's loss to the Eagles. Sinnott still played behind blocking tight end John Bates, but Sinnott profiles better to take on Okonkwo's receiving role. The 2024 second-round pick hasn't had much opportunity to produce in games so far, with only two career games above a 60% snap rate and 16 career receptions. Sinnott projects as a dart throw in a projected high-scoring Week 2 matchup against the Cowboys, ranking as RotoBaller's TE37 in PPR leagues.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Bigger role on tap
metadata.description: Sinnott should operate in an elevated role in the Commanders' offense against the Cowboys on Sunday after Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) was ruled out.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott did not see a target from Jayden Daniels during the Commanders' Week 1 loss to the Eagles, with the former playing 18 snaps on offense. John Bates is expected to be the Commanders' TE1 in Okonkwo's absence, but Sinnott -- who drew praise from the coaching staff for his development during training camp -- should also operate in an elevated role against Dallas.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott One to Watch on the Waiver Wire
metadata.description: Washington Commanders tight end Ben Sinnott did not record a single statistic in Week 1. The Commanders lost to the Philadelphia Eagles by a final score of 24-22, but Sinnott was a non-factor in the passing game. According to Pro Football Focus, Sinnott played 18 offensive snaps and 16 snaps on special teams. He played well behind Chig Okonkwo (hamstring), who had 39 offensive snaps, and John Bates, who had 34 offensive snaps. Okonkwo and Bates recorded two receptions each. Sinnott has amassed just 16 receptions for 142 yards and two touchdowns throughout his NFL career thus far, but he could have a slightly bigger role going into Week 2 action against the division-rival Dallas Cowboys if Okonkwo's hamstring injury keeps him out.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Doesn't record a stat
metadata.description: Sinnott played on 18 offensive snaps and 16 special-teams snaps but did not record a stat in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: The tight end was third in his positional rotation behind Chig Okonkwo (38 snaps) and John Bates (32). Sinnott caught 16 passes across his first two regular seasons in the NFL, but he has functioned mainly as a blocker in his professional career.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Full participant in Wednesday's practice
metadata.description: Sinnott (oblique) practiced in full Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott has been battling an oblique injury since the preseason. However, his full participation in Wednesday's practice suggests he is cleared to suit up for the Week 1 meeting with the Eagles. The 24-year-old appeared in 16 regular-season games for the Commanders in 2025, totaling 11 catches for 114 yards and one touchdown.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott (oblique) practices in full Wednesday
metadata.description: Ben Sinnott (oblique) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott recently suffered an oblique injury of some kind, but it's not a serious issue and he was still able to practice in a full capacity on Wednesday. He should be good to go for Week 1 but doesn't project to be a strong fantasy asset for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Sidelined for preseason finale
metadata.description: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said that Sinnott is dealing with an oblique injury and is unlikely to play in Friday's preseason finale versus the Ravens, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Sinnott won't practice this week after sustaining the injury this past Saturday. Quinn didn't indicate that the tight end's availability for the Commanders' Sept. 13 season opener versus the Eagles is in any peril, but Sinnott will likely need to return to full practice at some point over the next two-plus weeks to put himself on a path to play.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott (oblique) dealing with oblique injury
metadata.description: Ben Sinnott (oblique) is dealing with an oblique injury, per HC Dan Quinn.
metadata.analysis: The third year tight end is primarily a depth option at this point with little fantasy value. That's not to say he hasn't shown potential, he just needs to be given the role. It doesn't seem like that's coming anytime soon though.

metadata.title: Ben Sinnott - Running more routes in camp
metadata.description: Sinnott has run a wider variety of routes in training camp compared to previous years, though that is also the case for Washington's other tight ends, John Keim of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: New offensive coordinator David Blough is emphasizing versatility in his tight-end room, which includes Sinnott, Chig Okonkwo and John Bates, among others. Okonkwo is expected to get most of the pass-catching opportunities at the position. Sinnott hasn't shown much in that department, as the 2024 second-round pick has just 16 catches through 33 career regular-season games.
